note.text: Texture describes the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in fine earth. Structure describes particle aggregation. Porosity concerns pore volume; permeability concerns water movement through connected pores. Clay can hold much water yet drain slowly. Soil pH below 7 is acidic, around 7 neutral and above 7 alkaline under the usual reference conditions. Colour can suggest organic matter, minerals or drainage conditions but cannot establish fertility on its own. No single property gives a complete suitability assessment.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish texture structure porosity and chemical reaction and calculate a missing particle fraction. Builds on: soil components and pore contents. Leads to: reading a soil profile and explaining erosion risk.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Compare an aggregated garden soil with a compacted path near a Bamenda school. Similar mineral texture does not guarantee the same structure or infiltration. In a simplified laboratory record, the sand, silt and clay masses account for the entire stated fine-earth sample. This bookkeeping task is not enough to assign a formal texture-class name without the relevant classification chart.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State which property the evidence measures. Do not confuse particle size with aggregate arrangement, or water storage with rapid flow. A pH value describes reaction, not a direct score for every nutrient. Use the supplied masses consistently and leave out no fraction.

questions.prompt: A simplified dry fine-earth sample has mass {total} g: sand {sand} g, silt {silt} g, and the remainder clay. Find the clay mass.

misconceptions.explain: That is the combined sand and silt, not the remaining clay.
That leaves silt inside the supposed clay mass.
That reports the whole sample rather than its clay fraction.

solution: Add the sand and silt masses: {sand+silt} g.
Subtract from the complete sample: {total} − {sand+silt} = {answer} g.
